## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5956f4ba7048a5ca2943d12ce50b1dd66514ff48`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/triage-duties.md + scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/dispatch-runbook.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/filing-gate.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/instrument-discipline.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/skills.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/ui.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/cross-repo-coordination.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md

Director seat (summon #52, ledger objectstack#12708), summoned by the `domain:skills#1` seat for the second round (`5956f4ba`; the first round `c59cd9c6` was sent back by the seat for deleting three rules triage reads nowhere else). Read-only at this head: the diff, card #26667 (class ③, the maintainer's 「关于契约复审，开发自己有fable时都可以自己审核，只有开发的fable用完了，才需要分诊，但是此时分诊要能看出来，区别出来。」 and 「改进 skills」), the seat's ACCEPT 6446385869, the head tree (fetched; every deleted line's named home read with `git show` / `git grep`), the head's check runs. `.claude/**` ⇒ the rules face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; `record-recognisers.mjs` is the reader the rule names, in scope as one change with it. Tier S. Served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The rule under review governs this seat's own review path too (an exhausted tier here would hand off the same way); judged against the maintainer's words. The seat records; it does not approve, ready, queue or merge.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The ruling's seven points are encoded, each once.** (1) default unchanged — `contract-review.md:20` 「谁跑 = 派发席」 kept; (2) hand-off only on quota — `:21` 「派发席达档调用被配额拒(HTTP 429)⇒ ⛔ 不降档审;PR 落交接行、留等复核标记,交分诊席」; (3) the machine-findable shape — `:22` carries the card's line verbatim, and `:54` states the relation (label without the line = the seat's own, triage does not touch; head moved after the hand-off ⇒ new line or the seat's own review); (4) triage's act — `triage-duties.md:12–13` (newest line naming the current head; isolated at-tier subagent; same-shape record signed by the triage seat; own quota refusal written once, label kept, never lower); (6) stale tracking — `:14–17` (compare every own record's `Head-sha` to the current head, regen/prose-only excepted on the committed tree; stale FAIL re-reviewed the same round with every must-fix and the delta commits; stale PASS gets one note; round record `记录 head → 现 head → 状态`); (7) nothing lands on it — `:55` 「⛔ 无 check、workflow、队列守卫或巡查脚本读它」 kept, and the recogniser's pin shows `locateReviewOfRecord` reading FOUND past a hand-off line beside a record. Item 6's "expose `Head-sha` and `Reviewed-by`": answered by the existing `locateReviewOfRecord(...).sha` and `REVIEWED_BY_LINE` capture, as the claim's ONE-recogniser surface asks — no second reader. Right.
- **The recogniser is the rule, no wider.** `readContractReviewHandoff` requires the three facts (target `triage`, the tier by its constant NAME through the same token reader `Served-tier:` uses — a model id is unreadable here for the same reason it is there — reason and UTC time in the parentheses, a 7–40 hex head) and grades anything short as `unreadable`, never as a reading. `contractReviewHandoff` answers `absent` / `triage` / `stale` / `unreadable` off the newest line through `latestMarkedComment`, head matched by prefix like a record's span. 13 pins, including the four unreadable shapes, newest-governs both ways, decoration tolerance, and the no-gate pin. `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` 12 → 13 with the battery named. Consistent with the file's existing readers.
- **Every deleted line has the home the body names, on the head tree.** `contract-review.md` −2: the read-only shape and the input set live verbatim in the brief's built-in text (`record-recognisers.mjs:1368–1372`, pinned at `:2014–2016`) and in the `--template` `Local-runs:` note; the surviving `:37` points at that builtin. The readers line's filter query lives at `dispatch-runbook.md:44` 〈跨账户复审〉. `triage-duties.md` −6: emergency-triage authorization → `dispatch-runbook.md:11` 〈紧急卡直接分诊〉 (and `triage-duties.md:29` keeps the trigger); the three-exit first touch + `Batch-of:` → `filing-gate.md:25–28`; the three-state grading pointer → `filing-gate.md:46`; report-only instruments close → `instrument-discipline.md:8` and `:12` (ruling 208); lane seats do not triage → `lanes/skills.md:22`, `lanes/ui.md:8`, `cross-repo-coordination.md:31`; 域分批 / 积压告警 → `triage-duties.md:28` (kept) and `dispatch-runbook.md:27`. The three rules the first round had cut (the two (c)-metadata lines and 「⛔ 永不升级哪个仓的问题」) are back at `:40–42` and `:57`. No rule is lost; only pointers to homes this file already names.
- **Budget:** 55 / 103 lines, unchanged (ceilings 60 / 103). Six new triage lines 117 / 113 / 120 / 102 / 102 / 111 B; the hand-off line at `contract-review.md:22` is 122 B as ONE code span — the card's exact shape — and passes under the ratchet's `unbreakable` class (`check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs:2492, :2707`: a single code span has no legal wrap, so the gate never demands one). `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is green on this head, so that is the gate's reading, not only the dev's.
- **The quota case is the only trigger**, as the maintainer narrowed it: `:21` names 「配额拒(HTTP 429)」 and nothing else; a seat whose tier works has no path to triage. Right.

### ② Semver level

`.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` publish nothing; `skip-changeset`; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body. No level owed. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed path (`.claude/**`, Tier S): no approval yet; draft; `os-zhuang`, `hotlong` requested through the relay. This seat's account is not a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` member; this record is not an approval. With this PASS record on the head and green checks, the Tier S landing condition is met; ready/queue stay with the lane seat.
- Check runs on `5956f4ba`: 26 `success` (incl. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` — `check:pm-record-recognisers` — `Lint · repo & tooling gates` — the line ratchet — `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the PR-body guards, `Test Core` ×3, `Test UI`, `Type Check` ×4), 16 expected skips, 0 pending, 0 red.
- **Should-fix, out of this card's surface (the seat's open question ②):** `landing-operations.md:13` 「子代理起不来 ⇒ 复核缺席…旁路仅维护者逐次亲审」 still reads as if a review that cannot start has one bypass. It does not contradict the arm — a hand-off produces a record, it is not a bypass — but a reader of that line alone will not learn the quota case has a route. A one-line pointer there after this lands, as the seat proposes.
- Dev deviations: the 122-byte code span (judged above); the rulebook-reading pin dropped because `check:pm-dispatch-gates` classifies a script's structural read of a governed file as a census — the right call, the battery pins rows and strings only.
- The record shape triage will render is this one; a triage-signed record on a handed-off PR is read by the queue guard exactly as a seat's. Nothing in the diff gives the hand-off line any landing effect.

### ④ Design judgment

- `contract-review.md:20–22, :54` against the maintainer's words and the scenario (a dispatching seat's at-tier call returns 429 with a PR waiting on review): the seat has one act — post the line, keep the label — and no permission to review lower; triage can tell the case from a label alone because the line, not the label, is the hand-off, and a head that moves voids it. Holds; the only way to break it is to omit a fact from the line, and the recogniser answers `unreadable` rather than guessing.
- `triage-duties.md:12–17` against the #26598 incident (a stale FAIL on a moved head): the round step compares records to heads by the recogniser's own `Head-sha` read, treats a stale FAIL as owed in the same round and a stale PASS as a note, and writes the three-state line into the round record so a moved head cannot drop out of sight. The regen/prose-only exception reuses the existing committed-tree rule rather than a new one. Holds.
